editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. There are three small problems. [7] uses the formal "Travaillez" where every other card uses "tu" imperatives (Construis, Réduis, Filtre). The terms drift: "addons" in [0] but "extensions" everywhere else, and "error mitigation" is "atténuation des erreurs" in [15] but "mitigation d'erreurs" in [29]/[30], with "Mitigation des mesures" in [26]. Some headings are also calqued or unclear: "Découvrir les modèles de bruit" hides that the section is about noise learning, and "Correspondance de problèmes du domaine" and "Fonctionnalités de support" read stiffly.

examples.source: Work with fermionic systems using data structures...
examples.translation: Travaillez avec des systèmes fermioniques...
examples.suggested: Travaille avec des systèmes fermioniques...
examples.why: Formal vous imperative; every other card uses tu.

examples.source: Matrix-free Measurement Mitigation (M3)

examples.why: [15] and the card's own description use atténuation/atténue, but [29]/[30] use mitigation. Pick one; 'atténuation' is the standard French term.

examples.source: Learn noise models
examples.translation: Découvrir les modèles de bruit
examples.suggested: Apprendre les modèles de bruit
examples.why: The heading means characterizing (learning) noise models, not the reader discovering them. The body in [15] correctly says 'apprendre et affiner'.

examples.source: Overview of all Qiskit addons
examples.translation: Vue d'ensemble de tous les addons Qiskit
examples.suggested: Vue d'ensemble de toutes les extensions Qiskit

examples.translation: Correspondance de problèmes du domaine
examples.suggested: Traduire les problèmes métier en problèmes quantiques
examples.why: Stiff calque of 'mapping'; a French technical writer would use a verb-led heading.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and it keeps the informal "tu" throughout ("Découvre", "Consulte"). Core terms are correct and used the same way each time: "atténuation des erreurs", "valeurs d'espérance", "propagation de Pauli", "annulation probabiliste des erreurs (PEC)" and "mieux borner la sensibilité aux erreurs".

The meaning is faithful throughout. The required and optional inputs, the wholesale replacement of estimator_options, the 6073 per-job limit, the batching arithmetic and the reconnect caveats all match the English, and the file keeps "tu" consistently. A few spots are calqued or stiff: "fonctionnalités auxquelles tu peux souscrire" for "opt into" in [38], "réaffirmés" for restating config options in [64], "face à un QPU réel" in [42], and the awkward "Renomme le dossier extrait, de ce long nom, en" in [20]. The link text "[Job limits]" in [60] is left in English, while every other link label on the page is translated.

examples.source: the rest of the table is the functionality you can opt into

examples.suggested: le reste du tableau regroupe les fonctionnalités que tu peux activer au besoin

examples.source: dynamical decoupling and TREX are restated in the following cell to keep them switched on

examples.suggested: le découplage dynamique et TREX sont redéfinis explicitement dans la cellule suivante pour qu'ils restent activés
examples.why: 'Réaffirmer' means asserting a statement again. It is a calque of 'restated' and is not used for configuration options.

examples.translation: L'`EstimatorV2` atténué face à un QPU réel
examples.suggested: L'`EstimatorV2` atténué exécuté sur un QPU réel

examples.source: Rename the extracted folder from that long name to `source_files`.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 44 is faithful and idiomatic: "Alternative : exécuter l'exemple avec un simulateur" keeps the note's meaning, uses the correct French spacing before the colon, and matches the infinitive heading style used elsewhere ("Exécuter avec les primitives quantiques").

The meaning is faithful throughout. The shots/cost scaling, the Estimator precision note (which follows the English as written), the stale-noise-model caveat for NoiseLearner and the "tu" register are all intact. The one problem is the page description [0]. It renders "amount of usage spent" as "le temps utilisé consacré", which stacks two past participles and reads as a clumsy calque. A native editor would rewrite it as "le temps consommé par le traitement et l'exécution d'un job".

examples.source: How to minimize the amount of usage spent processing and running a job.
examples.translation: Comment minimiser le temps utilisé consacré au traitement et à l'exécution d'un job.
examples.suggested: Comment minimiser le temps consommé par le traitement et l'exécution d'un job.
examples.why: 'le temps utilisé consacré' puts two participles side by side. It reads as a literal calque of 'usage spent' and is awkward French.

editor_note: Entry 11 is faithful and reads naturally. The blocking caveat survives as "appel bloquant jusqu'à la fin", and "atteigne un état terminal" is correct for "reaches a terminal state". Using "état" in this entry while nearby prose says "statut" is a defensible choice.

The translation is faithful and reads naturally. It keeps the caveat that Qiskit 1.0 "rompt la compatibilité avec toutes les versions précédentes", renders "Breaking package changes" as "Modifications incompatibles du paquet", and uses "tu" throughout ("Consulte", "ton projet").

Entry 33 keeps the English meaning. X.Y.Z maps to majeur.mineur.révision, a revision change still guarantees the circuit runs, and the caveat that a major or minor change carries no guarantee but may still work ("bien que cela puisse être le cas") is kept. The one problem is style: "Un circuit compilé ... est garanti de fonctionner" copies the English "is guaranteed to run" word for word, and a native French technical writer would not put it that way. The last sentence of the same entry already uses the correct impersonal form ("il n'est pas garanti que le circuit fonctionne"). The feminine "cette QPU" matches how the page mostly treats QPU.

examples.source: A circuit compiled for a given version number is guaranteed to run on that QPU.
examples.translation: Un circuit compilé pour un numéro de version donné est garanti de fonctionner sur cette QPU.
examples.suggested: Un circuit compilé pour un numéro de version donné fonctionnera à coup sûr sur cette QPU. (ou : Il est garanti qu'un circuit compilé pour un numéro de version donné s'exécute sur cette QPU.)
examples.why: "être garanti de + infinitive" with a thing as the subject copies the English structure. Standard French uses the impersonal "il est garanti que" or "est assuré de". The meaning is correct, so this is a style fix only.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. Every entry says what the English says, including "chiffrées au repos", "menu contextuel" for the overflow menu, the Manager-role condition in [8], and the three-year retention caveat in [10]. The informal "tu" register holds throughout. The one fix is in entry [7]: the comma sits inside the link text ("[page Instances,]"), so it gets underlined as part of the link. It belongs after the closing parenthesis.

examples.source: from the [Instances page](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/instances), find the instance
examples.translation: depuis la [page Instances,](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/instances) trouve l'instance
examples.suggested: depuis la [page Instances](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/instances), trouve l'instance
examples.why: The comma has moved inside the link text, so it is rendered as part of the link. In the English it comes after the link.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner, and the informal tu register holds throughout ("crée", "Consulte", "Lis"). Two renderings read as literal calques. The heading "Répartir la tâche entre les travailleurs" translates "workers" word for word, but in French distributed-computing writing people keep "workers" or say "nœuds de calcul". In [5], "suivis par rapport au job Qiskit Serverless parent" calques "tracked against"; "rattachés au job parent" is the natural French for this.

examples.source: Distribute task across workers
examples.translation: Répartir la tâche entre les travailleurs
examples.suggested: Répartir la tâche entre les workers
examples.why: 'travailleurs' is a word-for-word calque of 'workers'. French developers keep 'workers' (or say 'nœuds de calcul') in distributed computing.

examples.source: so that the IBM Quantum Compute Service jobs and sessions it launches are tracked against the parent Qiskit Serverless job
examples.translation: afin que les jobs et sessions du service de calcul IBM Quantum® qu'il lance soient suivis par rapport au job Qiskit Serverless parent
examples.suggested: afin que les jobs et sessions du service de calcul IBM Quantum® qu'il lance soient rattachés au job Qiskit Serverless parent
examples.why: 'suivis par rapport au' calques 'tracked against' and reads stiffly. 'rattachés au' says the intended thing, that the jobs are attributed to the parent job.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the meaning. In 47 the negation ("il n'est pas vrai que chaque boucle… soit incluse") and the lattice-line caveat are correct, and in 48 the even-parity condition and the claim "toujours contenues dans le stabilisateur" match the English. The problem is terminology. Entry 47 defines the term « ligne de réseau horizontale/verticale », but entry 48 immediately switches to "ligne horizontale et chaque ligne verticale de qubits" and then to "ligne du réseau", so the term just defined never appears. There is also a small wording slip: 48 renders "shrunk to the identity" as "réduites à rien", which drops the mention of the identity operator (though it matches [53]'s "réduite à rien"), and "effectivement réduites" mistranslates the English "effectively" (French "effectivement" means "actually/indeed").

examples.source: an even number of qubits on every horizontal lattice line and every vertical lattice line
examples.translation: un nombre *pair* d'erreurs $X$ sur chaque ligne horizontale et chaque ligne verticale de qubits
examples.suggested: un nombre *pair* de qubits affectés sur chaque ligne de réseau horizontale et chaque ligne de réseau verticale
examples.why: Entry 47 has just defined « ligne de réseau horizontale/verticale » for exactly this sentence. Using a different wording right away weakens that clarification.

examples.source: they can effectively be shrunk to the identity by multiplying them by $X$ stabilizer generators
examples.translation: elles peuvent être effectivement réduites à rien en les multipliant par des générateurs de stabilisateurs $X$
examples.suggested: elles peuvent en pratique être réduites à l'identité en les multipliant par des générateurs de stabilisateurs $X$
examples.why: In French, 'effectivement' means 'actually/indeed', not 'effectively', and 'réduites à rien' drops the precise mention of the identity operator. Not misleading, but a native editor would change it.

editor_note: Faithful, natural French that uses tu correctly ("te guide", "Télécharge les diapositives") and keeps its terms consistent: "formalisme des stabilisateurs", "codes stabilisateurs", "code à répétition", "observables de matrices de Pauli".

Neither rewritten entry changes the meaning, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Entry 17 is clean: "sous-traitant de données tiers" is the correct GDPR term for "data processor", and it keeps the informal "te/tes" register. Entry 9 keeps the English sentence structure too closely. It pushes the passive "peut être considérée" to the end of a long clause, drops the article in "entre états quantiques" (it should be "entre les états quantiques"), and uses the calque "comment elles se rapportent aux canaux" where "la manière dont elles se rattachent aux canaux" would be more natural. The terms "matrices densité", "canaux" and "mesures" are correct and consistent.

examples.source: The course also discusses mathematical ways of formalizing the distance or similarity between quantum states, and how they relate to channels and measurements in operational ways.
examples.translation: Le cours aborde également les façons mathématiques de formaliser la *distance* ou la *similarité* entre états quantiques, et comment elles se rapportent aux canaux et aux mesures de manière opérationnelle.
examples.suggested: Le cours aborde également les manières de formaliser mathématiquement la *distance* ou la *similarité* entre les états quantiques, ainsi que la façon dont elles se rattachent, sur le plan opérationnel, aux canaux et aux mesures.
examples.why: The article is missing before 'états quantiques', 'façons mathématiques' is a calque, and 'et comment elles…' coordinated with a noun phrase is clumsy English-style syntax.

examples.source: and a more general class of measurements can be considered than those discussed in Basics of quantum information.
examples.translation: et une classe de *mesures* plus générale que celles discutées dans *Bases de l'information quantique* peut être considérée.
examples.suggested: et l'on peut envisager une classe de *mesures* plus générale que celles présentées dans *Bases de l'information quantique*.
examples.why: Putting the passive verb at the end of a long comparative clause reads stiffly. An active 'on peut envisager' placed first is more idiomatic and keeps the same meaning.

editor_note: Faithful and natural, with correct, consistent terms (channels→canaux, noisy communication channels→canaux de communication bruités, discrete-time→en temps discret, including the tooltip) and the informal tu register ("te guide", "Télécharge").

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: [70] keeps the superposition contrast ("contrairement à leurs homologues classiques… peuvent être en une superposition de 0 et 1 simultanément") and renders CLOPS as "opérations de couches de circuit par seconde", keeping the classical-interfacing caveat. [108] "Estimer la taille de la base de données et le temps nécessaire pour vérifier chaque élément" matches the English exactly.

The meaning is faithful throughout: the 20-question and 16-correct threshold, the lock after two failed attempts, and the Credly privacy notice all match the English. Nothing here would mislead a learner. Entry [8] has a grammar error: "tu dois en répondre correctement au moins 16" is wrong because "répondre" takes "à", not "en". Also, the survey is called "Enquête" in heading [4] but "sondage" in body [5], and "Félicitations pour avoir terminé" reads less idiomatically than "Félicitations d'avoir terminé".

examples.source: you must answer at least 16 correctly to pass
examples.translation: tu dois en répondre correctement au moins 16 pour réussir
examples.suggested: tu dois répondre correctement à au moins 16 d'entre elles pour réussir
examples.why: 'répondre' takes 'à', so 'en répondre' is ungrammatical. A native editor would rephrase it.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course! ... [quick survey]

examples.suggested: Félicitations d'avoir terminé ce cours ! ... [court questionnaire]

editor_note: The meaning is faithful and nothing would mislead a learner. The 20 questions, the 16-correct pass mark, the lock after two failed attempts and the Credly data-sharing caveats are all kept, and informal "tu" holds throughout. A few phrasings still need a native editor's touch. In [8], "tu dois en répondre correctement à au moins 16" is ungrammatical (répondre à does not take "en"). "Note de passage" in [8] and [9] is a calque of "passing score". "Réclamer ton badge" in [12] is an anglicism for "claim". In [12] the period has also moved inside the link text ("[ici.]").

examples.source: you must answer at least 16 correctly to pass
examples.translation: tu dois en répondre correctement à au moins 16 pour réussir
examples.suggested: tu dois répondre correctement à au moins 16 d'entre elles pour réussir
examples.why: "En répondre à" is ungrammatical: the pronoun "en" cannot work with "répondre à".

examples.source: If you don't receive a passing score in two attempts
examples.translation: Si tu n'obtiens pas une note de passage en deux tentatives
examples.suggested: Si tu n'obtiens pas la note minimale requise en deux tentatives
examples.why: "Note de passage" copies the English "passing score". In [8], "Après avoir obtenu une note de passage" should read "Une fois l'examen réussi".

examples.source: instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: les instructions pour réclamer ton badge
examples.suggested: les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: "Réclamer" here is an anglicism for "claim". In French it suggests demanding something you are owed, so "récupérer" or "accepter" is idiomatic.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course!
examples.translation: Félicitations pour avoir terminé ce cours !
examples.suggested: Félicitations d'avoir terminé ce cours !
examples.why: "Félicitations d'avoir terminé" is the more idiomatic construction.

editor_note: Entry [205] reverses the Bloch-sphere geometry of amplitude damping. The English says the region shrinks along the XY plane "to a lesser extent than along Z", while the French says "dans une moindre mesure le long de Z", which tells learners the opposite. The rest is faithful and mostly natural. Minor issues: the register often slips to vous ("Notez", "Observez", "Remarquez" in [86], [100], [122], [181], [207], [227], [253], [292]). Some terms are inconsistent: "matrice de densité" and "matrice densité", "bit-flips" and "bascule de bit", "étalonnage" and "calibration". In [187], "se désintègrent" is a poor choice for spontaneous decay to a lower energy level.

examples.source: shrunken both along the $Z$ axis, as well as along the $XY$ plane, though to a lesser extent than along $Z$.
examples.translation: contractée à la fois le long de l'axe $Z$ et le long du plan $XY$, bien que dans une moindre mesure le long de $Z$.
examples.suggested: contractée à la fois le long de l'axe $Z$ et dans le plan $XY$, bien que dans une moindre mesure que le long de $Z$.
examples.why: The comparison is reversed. The source says the XY plane shrinks less than Z, but the French says Z shrinks less, which misdescribes how the amplitude-damping channel deforms the state.

examples.source: Secondly, note that the off-diagonal elements... note what happens as $p\rightarrow 1$.
examples.translation: Deuxièmement, notez que les éléments hors diagonale... observez ce qui se passe lorsque $p\rightarrow 1$.
examples.suggested: Deuxièmement, note que les éléments hors diagonale... observe ce qui se passe lorsque $p\rightarrow 1$.
examples.why: This is a formal vous imperative in a page that otherwise uses tu. The same slip recurs in [86], [100], [122], [181], [207], [253] and [292].

examples.source: Sometimes quantum states will simply spontaneously decay from a higher energy level to a lower one.
examples.translation: Parfois, les états quantiques se désintègrent simplement et spontanément d'un niveau d'énergie plus élevé vers un niveau plus bas.
examples.suggested: Parfois, les états quantiques se désexcitent (relaxent) simplement et spontanément d'un niveau d'énergie plus élevé vers un niveau plus bas.
examples.why: In French, 'se désintégrer' suggests particle or nuclear disintegration. For energy relaxation the usual verb is 'se désexciter', which [91] already uses.

examples.source: density matrix
examples.translation: matrice densité
examples.suggested: matrice de densité
examples.why: Entries [114]-[176] use 'matrice de densité', but from [193] onward the page switches to 'matrice densité'. 'bit-flip' ([22]) and 'bascule de bit' ([228]) are also mixed within the file.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The conditions all match the English: 20 questions, at least 16 correct to pass, and a temporary lock after two failed attempts. The informal "tu" is used throughout. A native editor would still fix a few calques. In the privacy notice, "processeur de données tiers" copies "data processor"; the standard French privacy-law term is "sous-traitant". Also, "le cours … par IBM" should be "d'IBM", and "naviguer vers IBM Training" and "l'examen de badge" read as literal translations.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un processeur de données tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.suggested: un sous-traitant tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.why: In French privacy and GDPR language, 'data processor' is 'sous-traitant'. 'Processeur de données' is a literal calque.

examples.source: the "Use a quantum computer today" course by IBM®
examples.translation: le cours « Utiliser un ordinateur quantique aujourd'hui » par IBM® !
examples.suggested: le cours « Utiliser un ordinateur quantique aujourd'hui » d'IBM® !
examples.why: 'par IBM' copies the English 'by' word for word. Idiomatic French says 'le cours d'IBM'.

examples.source: click the button below to navigate to IBM Training, where you can take the badging exam
examples.translation: clique sur le bouton ci-dessous pour naviguer vers IBM Training, où tu peux passer l'examen de badge
examples.suggested: clique sur le bouton ci-dessous pour accéder à IBM Training, où tu pourras passer l'examen permettant d'obtenir le badge
examples.why: 'naviguer vers' and 'examen de badge' are stiff literal translations. 'Accéder à' and a phrase like 'l'examen permettant d'obtenir le badge' read more naturally.

editor_note: Entry 5 is faithful and reads naturally: "Ce cours est basé sur un cours donné en direct à l'Université de Tokyo" keeps both the live-course framing and the University of Tokyo attribution, and it matches entry 0's wording.

The course titles are translated faithfully and read naturally. The terminology is conventional: "Correction d'erreurs quantiques" for error correction, "Conception d'algorithmes variationnels" for Variational Algorithm Design, and "Utiliser un ordinateur quantique aujourd'hui" for "Use A Qc Today", where the "Qc" abbreviation is expanded correctly.

The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner, but entry [5] has a few calques. "the free time allotted" became "le temps libre alloué", and in French "temps libre" means leisure time, so it should read "le temps gratuit alloué". "can be completed" is rendered twice as "peut être complété(es)", where "réalisé(es)" or "terminé(es)" is more natural. In [4], "mécanique quantique introductive" is stiff; "un cours d'introduction à la mécanique quantique" reads better.

examples.source: in much less time than the free time allotted as part of the Open Plan
examples.translation: en beaucoup moins de temps que le temps libre alloué dans le cadre du forfait Open
examples.suggested: en beaucoup moins de temps que le temps gratuit alloué dans le cadre du forfait Open
examples.why: 'temps libre' means leisure time in French; the source means free-of-charge compute time.

examples.source: but can be completed independently or in small groups. All activities can be completed
examples.translation: mais peut être complété de manière indépendante ou en petits groupes. Toutes les activités peuvent être complétées
examples.suggested: mais peut être terminé en autonomie ou en petits groupes. Toutes les activités peuvent être réalisées
examples.why: 'compléter' in the sense of 'finish' is an anglicism; 'terminer' or 'réaliser' is idiomatic.

examples.source: or introductory quantum mechanics
examples.translation: ou en mécanique quantique introductive
examples.suggested: ou d'introduction à la mécanique quantique
examples.why: 'introductive' is a stiff, calqued adjective in this position.

editor_note: Entry 76 is faithful: "Quelle superposition d'états computationnels correspondrait à une QFT avec des pics sur chaque nombre binaire impair ?" keeps "odd" (impair), matches the answer in entry 77, and uses "état computationnel" the same way entry 53 does.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. Entry 178 keeps the upper-bound caveat ("borne supérieure") and the "légèrement inférieure" outcome intact, and entry 204 correctly says "l'énergie de réaction … est négative … de l'énergie est libérée" with "deux atomes séparés".
The three navigation entries are correct and idiomatic: Modules, Computer Science as Informatique and Quantum Mechanics as Mécanique quantique, with every link path left unchanged.

Neither rewritten entry misleads a learner. Entry 21 keeps its meaning, including the same-axis anti-correlation and the free-axis contrast. Entry 29 is faithful, uses the correct "tu" register, and needs no change. Entry 21 does have two wording problems a native editor would fix. "into the page" is rendered as "vers la page", which is not how French physics texts describe this direction; they say "rentrant dans la page" / "sortant de la page". In "l'un mesure up, l'autre mesure down", the bare English results are awkward after "mesure"; "l'un obtient up (spin haut)" would read better.

examples.line_approx: every time one measures into the page

examples.why: "vers la page" is a calque and a vague way to say "into the page". French physics texts say "rentrant" and "sortant" for directions perpendicular to the page.

examples.line_approx: every time one measures up, the other measures down

examples.translation: chaque fois que l'un mesure up, l'autre mesure down
examples.suggested: chaque fois que l'un obtient up, l'autre obtient down
examples.why: "mesurer up" copies the English sentence structure. "obtenir" is the natural French verb for a measurement result, and it matches the "spin up / spin down" wording in entry 17.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. The negations in the true/false questions, the little-endian explanation, the CNOT/Toffoli conventions and the half-adder logic all match the source. The problem is the Qiskit patterns step names. The list [168]-[171] translates them (Correspondance, Optimisation, Exécution, Post-traitement), but the section headings [173] "Mapping", [189] "Optimizing" and [197] "Executing" stay in English, while [199] is "Post-traitement", and [222] lists them in English as Map/Optimize/Execute/Post-process. There are also several calques: "la mesure effondre leur état" (transitive "effondrer"), "l'autre est garanti d'être trouvé", "avec la chaîne de bits dominante étant `1011`" and "Pourquoi ou pourquoi pas ?".

examples.source: 2. Optimizing:
examples.translation: 2. Optimizing :
examples.suggested: 2. Optimisation :
examples.why: Step headings mix English (Mapping/Optimizing/Executing) and French (Post-traitement), and the list at [168]-[171] uses French names, so the four patterns steps are named inconsistently.

examples.source: measurement collapses their state and destroys the superposition
examples.translation: la mesure effondre leur état et détruit la superposition
examples.suggested: la mesure fait s'effondrer leur état et détruit la superposition
examples.why: 'Effondrer' is not used transitively in idiomatic French physics prose. 'Faire s'effondrer' or 'réduit le paquet d'onde' is the usual phrasing. The same calque appears in [160], [186], [220] and [231].

examples.source: the other is guaranteed to be found in the |1> state
examples.translation: l'autre est garanti d'être trouvé dans l'état |1>
examples.suggested: on est sûr de trouver l'autre dans l'état |1>
examples.why: This is a calque of the English passive 'is guaranteed to be'. A French writer would not phrase it this way.

examples.source: You should obtain a histogram with the dominant bitstring being `1011`:
examples.translation: Tu devrais obtenir un histogramme avec la chaîne de bits dominante étant `1011` :
examples.suggested: Tu devrais obtenir un histogramme dont la chaîne de bits dominante est `1011` :
examples.why: The participle 'étant' copies the English 'being' construction and reads as machine translation.

examples.source: Why or why not?
examples.translation: Pourquoi ou pourquoi pas ?
examples.suggested: Justifie ta réponse.
examples.why: This is a literal calque of an English formula. French teaching material would say 'Justifie ta réponse' or 'Pourquoi ?'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The Open Plan time claim, the simulator fallback and the prerequisites (2×2 matrices, some Python) all survive intact, and "de niveau licence" is a good rendering of "undergraduate". A native editor would still fix two calques. In [4], "peut être complété de façon indépendante" uses the anglicism "compléter" for "finish", where "réalisé en autonomie" or "terminé" is expected. In [7], "l'endroit dans un programme où chaque module pourrait être le plus efficace" is a stiff, word-for-word rendering of "where in a curriculum".

examples.source: but can be completed independently or in small groups
examples.translation: mais peut être complété de façon indépendante ou en petits groupes
examples.suggested: mais peut être réalisé en autonomie ou en petits groupes
examples.why: 'Compléter' meaning 'finish' is an anglicism. 'Réaliser' or 'terminer' reads natively.

examples.source: recommendations on where in a curriculum each module might be most effective
examples.translation: des recommandations sur l'endroit dans un programme où chaque module pourrait être le plus efficace
examples.suggested: des recommandations sur le moment du cursus où il sera le plus utile
examples.why: This is a calque of 'where in a curriculum'. A French teaching text would place a module at a point in time ('moment'), not at a place ('endroit').

editor_note: Rewritten entry 47 is faithful and idiomatic: "Mais en quoi les choses seraient-elles différentes pour notre pièce quantique ? Vérifions." keeps the conditional, the "pièce quantique" term used elsewhere in the file, and a natural "Vérifions" for "Let's check".

The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. The addons table in [6] has style problems. Descriptions keep English title case ("Diagonalisation Quantique par Échantillonnage", "Rétropropagation d'Opérateur", "Compilation Quantique Approximative"). The first row uses a tu-imperative ("Réduis la largeur…") while every other row is a noun phrase. "PEC sampling overhead" is rendered as "surcharge d'échantillonnage", but French QC writing normally says "surcoût d'échantillonnage".

examples.source: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization for ground state estimation
examples.translation: Diagonalisation Quantique par Échantillonnage pour l'estimation de l'état fondamental
examples.suggested: Diagonalisation quantique par échantillonnage pour l'estimation de l'état fondamental
examples.why: English title case carried into French. French only capitalizes the first word of a descriptive phrase. The same problem appears in the OBP, MPF, AQC and PNA rows.

examples.source: Reduce circuit width and depth by cutting gates and wires
examples.translation: Réduis la largeur et la profondeur du circuit en coupant des portes et des fils
examples.suggested: Réduction de la largeur et de la profondeur du circuit par découpe de portes et de fils
examples.why: This table cell describes the package. A tu-imperative reads as an instruction to the learner and doesn't match the noun-phrase style of the other rows.

examples.source: Shaded Lightcones for reducing PEC sampling overhead
examples.translation: Cônes de lumière ombrés pour réduire la surcharge d'échantillonnage PEC
examples.suggested: Cônes de lumière ombrés pour réduire le surcoût d'échantillonnage de la PEC
examples.why: In error-mitigation literature, 'overhead' is conventionally 'surcoût'. 'Surcharge' suggests overload rather than extra cost.

editor_note: Entry 32 renders "Step 0. Setup" as "Étape 0. Configuration", which is faithful, idiomatic and matches the "Étape 1/2/3/4" headings used elsewhere in the file, with the anchor kept intact.

Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful throughout, including the caveats in [95]-[101] about why fidelity can be worse today and the constant vs. linear depth scaling. The problems are minor wording ones. 'Mid-circuit measurements' is translated two ways: 'mesures en cours de circuit' in [6] and 'mesures en milieu de circuit' everywhere else. [99] copies the English too closely with 'La profondeur capture la mise à l'échelle logique'. In [103], 'kicked Ising' becomes 'Ising perturbé', which is not the standard term. [6] is also missing the non-breaking space before ';' that French typography requires.

examples.source: with mid-circuit measurements (MCMs) and classical feedforward;
examples.translation: avec des mesures en cours de circuit (MCMs) et du feedforward classique;
examples.suggested: avec des mesures en milieu de circuit (MCM) et du feedforward classique ;
examples.why: Every other entry ([11], [15], [95]) uses 'mesures en milieu de circuit'. French typography also needs a space before ';'.

examples.source: Depth captures the logical scaling of two-qubit operations
examples.translation: La profondeur capture la mise à l'échelle logique des opérations à deux qubits
examples.suggested: La profondeur rend compte de l'évolution logique du nombre d'opérations à deux qubits
examples.why: 'capture la mise à l'échelle' is a calque of the English. A native technical writer would write 'rend compte de' / 'traduit'.

examples.source: Simulation of kicked Ising Hamiltonian with dynamic circuits
examples.translation: Simulation du Hamiltonien d'Ising perturbé avec des circuits dynamiques
examples.suggested: Simulation de l'hamiltonien d'Ising pulsé (kicked Ising) avec des circuits dynamiques
examples.why: 'Kicked' means periodic pulsed driving, not a generic perturbation. 'perturbé' is recognizable but not the conventional term.

examples.source: impacts the number of operations
examples.translation: impacte le nombre d'opérations
examples.suggested: influe sur le nombre d'opérations
examples.why: 'impacter' is a common anglicism that careful French technical writing avoids.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The three approximations, the truncation trade-off and the differential meson minus vacuum protocol all match the English, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The issues are editorial. In [48], "layering" is rendered as "en superposant", which in a quantum text suggests superposition. In [47], "approximatif" agrees with "champ" instead of "énergie". Other slips: the calques "somme sur les sites" [30], "Résultats d'apprentissage" [5] and a dangling "tout au long" [33]; one formal "Votre" [4] where the page uses "tu"; and "fermions décalés" for staggered fermions, where "fermions alternés" is the more usual French term.

examples.source: layering interaction, electric, and mass terms with SWAP gates
examples.translation: en superposant les termes d'interaction, électrique et de masse avec des portes SWAP
examples.suggested: en empilant par couches les termes d'interaction, électrique et de masse, avec des portes SWAP
examples.why: In a quantum computing text, 'superposer' reads like quantum superposition. The English only means stacking layers.

examples.source: the approximate electric field energy at each site
examples.translation: l'énergie du champ électrique approximatif à chaque site
examples.suggested: l'énergie approximative du champ électrique sur chaque site
examples.why: The adjective agrees with 'champ' (masculine), so the French calls the field approximate. In the English it is the energy that is approximated.

examples.source: where $\{r'\}$ sums over sites in the fermionic configuration
examples.translation: où $\{r'\}$ somme sur les sites dans la configuration fermionique
examples.suggested: où la somme sur $\{r'\}$ porte sur les sites dans la configuration fermionique
examples.why: 'somme sur' used as a verb is a calque of the English. A French physics writer would say 'la somme porte sur'.

examples.source: Your runtime may vary.
examples.translation: Votre temps d'exécution peut varier.
examples.suggested: Ton temps d'exécution peut varier.
examples.why: Formal 'Votre' breaks the informal 'tu' register used everywhere else on the page.

examples.source: We fix $\delta_\tau = 0.0015$ throughout.
examples.translation: Nous fixons $\delta_\tau = 0.0015$ tout au long.
examples.suggested: Nous fixons $\delta_\tau = 0.0015$ tout au long du tutoriel.
examples.why: 'tout au long' needs a complement in French. As written, the sentence is incomplete.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the truncation caveats in [18]/[60] and the "six groups, not eight" logic in [47], so nothing would mislead a learner. There are still a few things a native editor would fix. [51] has the non-word "transpitons" (should be "transpilons"). "Expectation value" is consistently the calque "valeur attendue", where French physics uses "valeur moyenne" or "espérance"; this makes [57] read "Comme attendu, les deux valeurs attendues concordent". The register mixes tu ("assure-toi", "tu verras", "Note également") with vous ("Notez" in [27], "Consultez" in [11]/[40]/[61]). [42] renders "separate basis measurement" as "mesure de base séparée", which can read as "basic measurement".

examples.source: Now we transpile both the original and the backpropagated circuits into the basis gate of the backend.
examples.translation: Nous transpitons maintenant les circuits original et rétropropagé dans la porte de base du backend.
examples.suggested: Nous transpilons maintenant les circuits original et rétropropagé vers les portes de base du backend.
examples.why: "transpitons" is a typo or non-word; the verb is "transpiler".

examples.source: As expected, the two expectation values agree.
examples.translation: Comme attendu, les deux valeurs attendues concordent.
examples.suggested: Comme prévu, les deux valeurs moyennes concordent.
examples.why: "valeur attendue" is a calque of "expectation value"; the conventional French term is "valeur moyenne" (or "espérance"). It is used consistently across the file, so this is minor.

examples.source: Note that in a noiseless simulator, the expectation value obtained with and without backpropagation will be same.
examples.translation: Notez que dans un simulateur sans bruit, la valeur attendue obtenue avec et sans rétropropagation sera la même.
examples.suggested: Note que dans un simulateur sans bruit, la valeur moyenne obtenue avec et sans rétropropagation sera la même.
examples.why: Vous-form slip; the page otherwise uses tu ("assure-toi", "tu verras", "Note également"). "Consultez" in [11], [40] and [61] has the same problem.

examples.source: so we need a separate basis measurement to calculate the expectation value of $IZ$
examples.translation: donc nous avons besoin d'une mesure de base séparée pour calculer la valeur attendue de $IZ$
examples.suggested: donc il faut une mesure dans une base distincte pour calculer la valeur moyenne de $IZ$
examples.why: "mesure de base" can read as "basic measurement"; the point is measuring in a different basis.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The PCE compression claims, n = O(m^{1/2}), the three measurement settings, the regularization parameters and the swap-search post-processing all match the English, and the core terms are consistent: valeur espérée, chaîne de Pauli, fonction de perte, plateaux stériles. The problems are native-editor fixes only. Entry [0] uses the formal "Utilisez", which breaks the "tu" convention. Entry [55] calques "material" as "le matériel suivant" and repeats "intéressé". "Near-term" becomes "actuel" in [7] and [12], and entry [33] calques "read as" as "se lit".

examples.source: Use Pauli correlation encoding to encode optimization problems...
examples.translation: Utilisez l'encodage par corrélation de Pauli pour encoder...
examples.suggested: Utilise l'encodage par corrélation de Pauli pour encoder...
examples.why: This is a formal vous-imperative, while the rest of the page uses informal tu (assure-toi, consulte, t'a intéressé).

examples.source: If you found this work interesting, you might be interested in the following material:
examples.translation: Si ce travail t'a intéressé, tu pourrais être intéressé par le matériel suivant :
examples.suggested: Si ce travail t'a plu, les ressources suivantes pourraient t'intéresser :
examples.why: "Matériel" is a calque of "material" and in French suggests hardware or equipment. The word "intéressé" is also repeated.

examples.source: on near-term quantum hardware
examples.translation: sur du matériel quantique actuel
examples.suggested: sur du matériel quantique à court terme (NISQ)
examples.why: "Near-term" is a recognized term of art. "Actuel" slightly changes the meaning to "current". The same shift happens in [12] ("dispositifs quantiques actuels").

examples.source: the number of qubits n needed to express a certain number of nodes m read as:
examples.translation: le nombre de qubits $n$ nécessaires pour exprimer un certain nombre de nœuds $m$ se lit :
examples.suggested: le nombre de qubits $n$ nécessaires pour représenter $m$ nœuds s'écrit :
examples.why: "Se lit" is a calque of "read as". "S'écrit" or "est donné par" is the idiomatic choice in French.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The ZNE/PEA/PEC explanations, the three amplification methods and the result-array axes all match the source. The main problem is register: the transpilation bullet list [58]-[61] and the extrapolated_noise_factors option [75] switch to "vous" (Choisissez, votre, Insérez, Traduisez, Effectuez, Spécifiez), while the rest of the page uses "tu". Smaller issues: "runtime error mitigation" is misparsed as "atténuation d'erreurs d'exécution" [42]. "Twirled" is rendered two ways, "couches twirl" [49] and "twirlées" [74]. The "primitives documentation" link text became a bare "ici" [67]. Expectation value is rendered consistently as "valeur attendue", which is a calque; "valeur moyenne" is the usual French physics term.

examples.source: Pick a qubit layout that maps the virtual qubits of your circuit to physical qubits on the hardware.
examples.translation: Choisissez une disposition de qubits qui associe les qubits virtuels de votre circuit à des qubits physiques sur le matériel.
examples.suggested: Choisis une disposition de qubits qui associe les qubits virtuels de ton circuit à des qubits physiques du matériel.
examples.why: Formal vous/votre breaks the page's tu convention. The same slip appears in [59]-[61] and [75].

examples.source: We will forgo this step since runtime error mitigation is not supported on simulators.
examples.translation: Nous allons ignorer cette étape car l'atténuation d'erreurs d'exécution n'est pas prise en charge par les simulateurs.
examples.suggested: Nous allons ignorer cette étape, car l'atténuation d'erreurs de Qiskit Runtime n'est pas prise en charge sur les simulateurs.
examples.why: 'Runtime' refers to the Qiskit Runtime service, not to execution errors. The practical conclusion is the same, but the phrase is misparsed.

examples.source: These define the three twirled layers you need to learn the noise for
examples.translation: Celles-ci définissent les trois couches twirl dont tu dois apprendre le bruit
examples.suggested: Celles-ci définissent les trois couches soumises au twirling dont tu dois apprendre le bruit
examples.why: 'couches twirl' is ungrammatical, and [74] uses 'twirlées' for the same idea, so the term is inconsistent.

examples.source: Find the broadcasting rules for primitives in the [primitives documentation](/guides/primitives).
examples.translation: Les règles de broadcasting pour les primitives sont disponibles [ici](/guides/primitives).
examples.suggested: Tu trouveras les règles de broadcasting des primitives dans la [documentation des primitives](/guides/primitives).
examples.why: The descriptive link text was replaced by a bare 'ici', so the reader loses the name of the target page.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The appendix conditions (geometric separation of about √N, classical complexity of about N, quantum complexity well below N) and the caveats in [13] come through intact, and the "tu" register holds. "Feature map" is rendered two ways: "carte de caractéristiques" in [12] and [41], but "mappage de caractéristiques (feature map)" in [35]. The two collide with "mappage de caractéristiques (feature mapping)" in [11], and "matrice de noyau"/"fonction de noyau" also alternate with "matrice noyau"/"fonction noyau" in [52]. A few spots are stiff calques: "frais d'échantillonnage" for "sampling overhead", "intègre" for "embeds" (the usual word is "plonge"), "Résultats d'apprentissage" and "Exemple de matériel à grande échelle".

examples.source: We now construct the feature map that embeds our classical dataset into a higher-dimensional feature space.
examples.translation: Nous construisons maintenant le mappage de caractéristiques (feature map) qui intègre notre jeu de données classique dans un espace de caractéristiques de dimension supérieure.
examples.suggested: Nous construisons maintenant la carte de caractéristiques (feature map) qui plonge notre jeu de données classique dans un espace de caractéristiques de dimension supérieure.
examples.why: [12] and [41] use 'carte de caractéristiques' for 'feature map', while [11] uses 'mappage' for the process 'feature mapping'. The standard French term for 'embed' in ML is 'plonger' (noun: 'plongement'), not 'intégrer'.

examples.source: leading to lower sampling overhead, improved robustness to hardware noise, and better scalability
examples.translation: ce qui entraîne une réduction des frais d'échantillonnage, une meilleure robustesse au bruit matériel et une meilleure évolutivité
examples.suggested: ce qui réduit le surcoût d'échantillonnage, améliore la robustesse au bruit matériel et facilite le passage à l'échelle
examples.why: 'Frais' sounds like a monetary cost. The idiomatic technical word for 'overhead' is 'surcoût', and 'passage à l'échelle' is the more natural rendering of 'scalability' here.

examples.source: The projected quantum kernel is defined with the following kernel function ... entries of the kernel matrix
examples.translation: défini avec la fonction noyau suivante ... les entrées de la matrice noyau
examples.suggested: fonction de noyau ... matrice de noyau
examples.why: [11] and [12] use 'matrice de noyau' / 'fonction de noyau'. The file should pick one form and use it throughout.

examples.source: Learning outcomes
examples.translation: Résultats d'apprentissage
examples.suggested: Objectifs d'apprentissage
examples.why: This is a literal calque. French course material conventionally says 'Objectifs d'apprentissage'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The Open Plan caveat in [27], the COBYLA noise explanation in [51] and the 100-node weighted-graph setup in [64] all keep their conditions and quantities intact. Core terms are consistent across the file: hamiltonien de coût, état fondamental, opérateur de mélange, circuit ansatz paramétré, transpiler, and shots. The one change an editor would make is in [76]. There "material" is calqued as "le matériel suivant", but in this file "matériel" consistently means hardware, and the sentence also repeats "intéress-" twice. "les ressources suivantes" would be clearer.

examples.source: If you found this work interesting, you might be interested in the following material:
examples.translation: Si ce travail t'a intéressé, le matériel suivant pourrait t'intéresser :
examples.suggested: Si ce travail t'a plu, ces ressources pourraient t'intéresser :
examples.why: "matériel" means hardware everywhere else on the page (exécution matérielle, Backend matériel), so it reads oddly for learning material. The repeated intéressé/intéresser is also clumsy.

editor_note: I found no meaning errors. HOBO/QUBO, the cubic terms, the 156-qubit Heron width, the ground-state goal and the comparison saying lower cost is better all match the English. There is one formal-register slip: [5] says "Votre temps d'exécution" where the page otherwise uses "tu". There are also a few calques: "il atteint des solutions précises" in [8] and "une fonction Qiskit par Q-CTRL Fire Opal" in [0]. The term is inconsistent too: "Qiskit Functions" is left in English in [15], but elsewhere it is "fonctions Qiskit".

examples.source: Your runtime might vary.
examples.translation: Votre temps d'exécution peut varier.
examples.suggested: Ton temps d'exécution peut varier.
examples.why: Formal 'votre' breaks the informal 'tu' convention used throughout the rest of the page.

examples.source: it achieves accurate solutions at utility scale
examples.translation: il atteint des solutions précises à l'échelle utilitaire
examples.suggested: il obtient des solutions précises à l'échelle utilitaire
examples.why: In French you 'atteint' a goal, not a solution; 'obtient' is the natural verb here.

examples.source: A Qiskit Function by Q-CTRL Fire Opal
examples.translation: une fonction Qiskit par Q-CTRL Fire Opal
examples.suggested: une fonction Qiskit de Q-CTRL Fire Opal
examples.why: 'par' for authorship/provenance calques English 'by'; the same phrase appears again in the link text in [7].

examples.source: Qiskit Functions (`pip install qiskit-ibm-catalog`)
examples.translation: Qiskit Functions (`pip install qiskit-ibm-catalog`)
examples.suggested: Fonctions Qiskit (`pip install qiskit-ibm-catalog`)
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'fonctions Qiskit' ([4], [20]), so leaving it in English here is inconsistent.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The clipping and ε=0.5 caveat, the ~49% p=1 limit, the energies −0.62/−0.74/−1.50 and the convergence-versus-sample distinction are all kept, and the terms are consistent (démarrage à chaud, mixeur, hamiltonien de coût, état fondamental, relaxation continue). A few English calques and one grammar slip remain. "écrête c*_i loin de 0 et 1" copies "clips away from", "chaque arête contribue un couplage" uses a transitive "contribuer", "Presque chaque tir" copies "nearly every shot", and "n'échantillonne que occasionnellement" is missing the elision "qu'occasionnellement".

examples.source: clips $c^*_i$ away from 0 and 1
examples.translation: écrête $c^*_i$ loin de 0 et 1
examples.suggested: écarte $c^*_i$ des valeurs 0 et 1 (en le bornant à $[\varepsilon, 1-\varepsilon]$)
examples.why: This copies the English "clip away from". In French, "écrêter loin de" does not read as a real construction.

examples.source: each edge contributes a $Z_i Z_j$ coupling of strength $+0.5$
examples.translation: chaque arête contribue un couplage $Z_i Z_j$ de force $+0.5$
examples.suggested: chaque arête apporte un couplage $Z_i Z_j$ d'intensité $+0.5$
examples.why: In French, "contribuer" does not take a direct object. This is an English calque.

examples.source: one that only occasionally samples the right answer
examples.translation: qu'un état qui n'échantillonne que occasionnellement la bonne réponse
examples.suggested: qu'un état qui n'échantillonne qu'occasionnellement la bonne réponse
examples.why: The elision is missing: "que" before a vowel must become "qu'".

examples.source: Nearly every shot returns the correct answer
examples.translation: Presque chaque tir renvoie la bonne réponse
examples.suggested: Presque tous les tirs renvoient la bonne réponse
examples.why: "Presque chaque" copies "nearly every". "Presque tous les" is the natural French wording, and entry 71 has the same pattern.
